name: Heart
blood_supply: Right and left coronary arteries, arising from the ascending aorta.
venous_drainage: Mainly cardiac veins draining to the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium.
innervation: Autonomic only, through the superficial and deep cardiac plexuses. Sympathetic fibres (pre-ganglionic from spinal segments T1-T4/5, relayed in the cervical and upper thoracic sympathetic ganglia) raise heart rate and force of contraction. Parasympathetic fibres from the vagus nerve (X) slow the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes. Visceral afferents carry cardiac pain with the sympathetic nerves, which is why it is felt in the chest, neck and left arm.

name: Right atrium
blood_supply: Right coronary artery (atrial branches); the sinoatrial nodal artery arises from it in about 60% of people and from the left circumflex artery in the rest.
venous_drainage: Anterior cardiac veins and the smallest (Thebesian) veins open directly into the atrium; the coronary sinus, which collects most cardiac veins, opens into it.
innervation: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic and vagal fibres); the sinoatrial node in its wall is the pacemaker, modulated by both. Visceral afferents travel with the sympathetic and vagal fibres.

name: Right ventricle

venous_drainage: Anterior cardiac veins drain directly into the right atrium; the small cardiac vein runs to the coronary sinus.
innervation: Cardiac plexus: sympathetic fibres from T1-T4/5 and vagal parasympathetic fibres; the conduction fibres (right bundle branch, Purkinje network) are modulated by these nerves.

name: Left atrium

venous_drainage: Small cardiac veins and the oblique vein of the left atrium (Marshall) drain to the coronary sinus. Blood does not drain through the four pulmonary veins; they bring oxygenated blood into the atrium.
innervation: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic and vagal fibres); volume (stretch) receptors in the atrial wall send afferents in the vagus nerve.

name: Left ventricle

venous_drainage: Great, middle and posterior cardiac veins drain to the coronary sinus; a small part drains through Thebesian veins directly into the cavity.
innervation: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibres from T1-T4/5, vagal parasympathetic fibres); mainly sympathetic control of contractility. Ischaemic pain is carried by sympathetic afferents.

name: Tricuspid valve
blood_supply: Valve leaflets are thin and almost avascular: they are nourished by diffusion from the blood passing over them. Small vessels from the adjacent myocardium (coronary branches) reach only the base of the leaflets and the valve ring. The ring is supplied by the right coronary artery.
venous_drainage: Any small vessels at the base of the leaflets drain to the anterior cardiac veins and the coronary sinus.
innervation: A sparse network of autonomic and sensory fibres from the cardiac plexus lies mostly at the base of the leaflets and the papillary muscles; the right ventricular conduction fibres run close by.

name: Pulmonary valve
blood_supply: Valve leaflets are thin and almost avascular: they are nourished by diffusion from the blood passing over them. venous_drainage: Any small vessels at the base of the cusps drain to the anterior cardiac veins.
innervation: A sparse network of autonomic and sensory fibres from the cardiac plexus, mostly at the base of the cusps.

name: Mitral valve
blood_supply: Valve leaflets are thin and almost avascular: they are nourished by diffusion from the blood passing over them. Small vessels from the adjacent myocardium (coronary branches) reach only the base of the leaflets and the valve ring. The ring is supplied by the left circumflex artery; the papillary muscles receive blood from the left anterior descending and the circumflex or right coronary arteries (the posteromedial one often from a single artery, so it is ischaemia-prone).
venous_drainage: Any small vessels at the base of the leaflets drain to the great cardiac vein and the coronary sinus.
innervation: A sparse network of autonomic and sensory fibres from the cardiac plexus, mostly at the base of the leaflets and the papillary muscles.

venous_drainage: Superficial cerebral veins to the superior sagittal and other dural venous sinuses; deep cerebral veins to the great cerebral vein and the straight sinus; all drain through the sigmoid sinuses to the internal jugular veins.
